About Slamhaus

Slamhaus is a small, opinionated web tool for people who think in systems, tools, levels, simulations, and source files. It keeps content in Markdown and puts browser behavior in typed, game-oriented C++.

The idea

Most static-site tools are built around a scripting ecosystem. Most frontend tools assume the browser is the centre of the universe. Slamhaus takes a third route: treat a website like a buildable project.

Pages are source files. Routes are data. Components are declarations. C++ is an optional behavior module. The compiler turns those pieces into a complete, inspectable website without asking a runtime to stay alive after deployment.

The build pipeline

The pipeline is deliberately visible: each stage has a narrow job and produces an inspectable hand-off for the next one.

01 / source Markdown + .slam
02 / understand parse + validate
03 / compose route + render
04 / optional C++ → Emscripten
05 / ship atomic dist/

The result above is a real Slam UI component, not a decorative image. Its layout is responsive CSS, its labels are generated semantic HTML, and its optional WebAssembly stage is shown as part of the same flow rather than as a separate product story.

A game-developer's web stack

Slamhaus borrows useful instincts from game development:

  • explicit data flow instead of ambient global state;
  • named systems with narrow responsibilities;
  • deterministic builds and reproducible toolchains;
  • small value types and clear ownership at boundaries;
  • a fast edit-check-build loop;
  • an escape hatch when the built-in primitive is not enough.

It does not pretend to be an engine. There is no scene graph, reflection system, garbage collector, proprietary renderer, or fake browser abstraction. The SDK gives you useful browser capabilities and leaves rendering choices to you.

Designed for real sites

Slamhaus validates missing pages, route collisions, unsafe paths, partial cycles, unsupported behavior adapters, and invalid component properties before replacing output. Generated HTML includes semantic regions, labels, live output, focus states, and responsive defaults. The result can be served from a folder, an object store, a CDN, or GitHub Pages.

The honest trade-offs

Slamhaus is a good choice if you value readable source, a small toolchain, C++ behavior, and a static deployment. It is not trying to replace a CMS, a mature JavaScript application framework, or a visual page builder. If you need a huge plugin marketplace or a client-side state graph with hundreds of screens, another tool may be the better fit.

Project status

The project is young and intentionally experimental, but its contracts are treated seriously: stable diagnostics, shared language specifications, pinned toolchains, automated tests, generated API documentation, and examples that exercise the real compiler.
